headline: Transcriptomic pipelines nominate candidate hub genes and biomarkers across diseases
label: Transcriptomic Hub Gene Biomarkers
summary: Public transcriptomic datasets and machine learning are now routinely combined with scRNA-seq and Mendelian randomization to prioritize candidate genes.
synthesis: The common thread is the prioritization of candidate genes and regulators from transcriptomic data, typically combining differential expression, WGCNA, PPI hub analysis, and machine learning with validation layers such as Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA-seq, or in vitro experiments. Most items are computational nominations rather than validated mechanisms. Several extend this framework in new directions: REN-former fine-tunes Geneformer on kidney scRNA-seq and uses in silico perturbation to predict directional state transitions, and a sparse Stabl-based pipeline is applied to cord blood multi-omic data for bronchopulmonary dysplasia. Sepsis recurs, with age- and severity-stratified ferroptosis analysis across 17 blood datasets and a mitochondria-focused machine learning study with scRNA-seq. Other items nominate specific genes such as PFKFB3, TLR2, CXCL9, MMP8, BRCA1, ADM, CFH, and TP53INP1, often framed as candidates for experimental follow-up.
